_about: LEARNING LARGE, Ryan's brief, 2026-10-03: a room about learning, making and knowledge gardening with generative AI, with the emphasis on our spiky profiles and how they can complement each other. Its tagline is his: Models are spiky. Humans are too. Learning, making, and knowledge gardening, together. It pulls its material from our AI hub, stimpunks.org/ai/, and the pages that hub maps, and it carries a rack with the latest month from AI channels he listed, which lives in data/learning-large-month.json because a timer refills it. tools/make-learning-large.py writes every quotation, the propagation diagram, the sowing log, the drawings, the bench screen and the rack, and holds the promises.
_pages: Every page the room quotes, with the file the Knowledge System mirror keeps it in, read on 2026-10-03. Every quotation in `quotes` names one of these, and make-learning-large.py looks for its words, word for word, in that file on every build, the Town Hall's rule about a page somebody else keeps: when the page changes, re-copy the quotation, never loosen the check. Without the mirror it says it could not check and carries on. A stimpunks.org address keeps its trailing slash, make-library.py's rule and that site's redirects'.

disability.title: AI, Disability Justice, and the Ethics of Making

_quotes: A QUOTATION IS WORDS ON ONE OF OUR PAGES, and nothing else. `said` is the words exactly as the page has them, typographic quotes and all; `page` is the key in `pages` it was read on. Most are our own sentences. Where the words are somebody else's, quoted on our page, `by` names them and `work` and `work_url` name what they wrote, and the room says the words were read on our page rather than in the original, the Community Library's rule: nobody here read the original for this room. A quotation is capped at `cap` words, Covenstead's reason rather than the Zibaldone's: a handful of passages the room is about, not a quote bank. Each one goes into the page between its own ll:quote markers, and the tool refuses a quotation with no marker or a marker with no quotation.

quotes.said: We build with these tools carefully and name what they are: not neutral, not magic, and not a replacement for the communities whose knowledge this site holds.
we are good at some things, bad at other things, and the difference between the two tends to be much greater than it is for most other people.
quotes.work: Autistic Skill Sets: A Spiky Profile of Peaks and Troughs

quotes.said: It is real, and it is why these tools matter to people with spiky profiles.
not on comparison with a polytropic norm but on assessment of the fit between cognitive architecture and environmental demands
quotes.work: Monotropic Artificial Intelligence: Toward a Cognitive Taxonomy of Domain-Specialized Language Models

quotes.said: People didn’t go to a sophist for wisdom. They went to a sophist to solve problems.
quotes.work: LLMs are bullshitters. But that doesn’t mean they’re not useful.

quotes.said: Ask a general-purpose chatbot about autism and you get the pathology paradigm back.

Different kinds of minds see different parts of the world. A competency network lets those different views work together. What one person misses, another catches. What one person can’t do, another can.
This is not about ranking people. It is not about who is better or worse. It is about fit, trust, and seeing each other clearly.
For many Autistic and otherwise Disabled people, AI is the scaffold that finally lets them say the true thing they could never get out unassisted.
Does this use make our competencies more legible to each other, or less?
it is not our place to judge whether someone’s needs are legitimate enough to use an ethically impure solution.
We want the people in our community to have the knowledge to protect themselves.
The warmth of the interface is a design choice. It is not evidence of personhood or concern.
EdTech produces data. MADTech produces artifacts.
Is the human the maker, or the subject?
The constructionist vision of AI is not a reaction to ChatGPT. It is the original vision. The extraction came later.
Everyone needs a prosthetic!
quotes.work: Our Roots: Logo, Piaget, and AI
quotes.via: as quoted by Gary Stager in

quotes.said: Writing is not transcription of thought that already exists. Writing is how the thinking gets made.
AI participates in the middle of the process, not at the beginning or end.
Generative AI can be part of that process, but the garden belongs to the community that cultivates it.
A spider is a guide to the garden, never a replacement for it.
Since generative AI uses knowledge taken from community, we offer all knowledge and writing derived with AI use to the commons
Different pages, one commitment: broken systems, not broken people — including the systems we build with.

_practices: THE PRACTICES ARE OUR COMPETENCY NETWORKS PAGE'S, WORD FOR WORD: the bold first sentence of each, in that page's order, under its own heading. Each is looked for in the mirror on every build. The rest of each practice is on that page, which the room links, because the room points at it rather than becoming a second copy of it.

practices.heading: Practices: Using AI to Increase Legibility Across the Team
items: Show the prompt, not just the polished output.
Use AI to surface your reasoning, not to stand in for it.
Do not outsource the first vulnerable move.
Body-double with AI in the open.
Run the legibility test before you send.

_diagram: THE KNOWLEDGE SYSTEM, our AI Collaboration page's own diagram, every step word for word and in its order, looked for in the mirror on every build. The room sets it as a propagation bench: `stage` says which part of the glasshouse each step happens in, and that grouping is ours, said so under it. The page's own sentence about it, that AI participates in the middle of the process and not at the beginning or end, is what the grouping follows.

stages.seed: The seed, before the lamp is switched on

_peaks: A MODEL'S PEAKS AND TROUGHS, AS OUR PAGES DESCRIBE THEM. Every line is ours and every one names the page that says it, by its key in `pages`, or `street` for How this site is made on this street. Nothing here is a benchmark or a claim of our own about any model: it is what our pages already say, gathered in one place, which is why each line links the page.

peaks.say: Translating knowledge across jargon and institutional silos into somebody's own words
Synthesising and connecting years of writing across many fields, and finding the patterns in it
Help without judgement, and without the cost of asking a person again
A scaffold for saying the true thing somebody could not get out unassisted

troughs.say: Truth: it produces likely text, with nothing in it that cares whether the text is accurate
Knowing where its competence ends: fluent on any topic, which looks like expertise
Disagreeing: trained in ways that pull it towards telling you what you want to hear
Our words for ourselves: the default corpus speaks about us, not as us
Communication that is variable, multimodal or state-dependent, as AAC and echolalia are
Writing from memory where a record was needed, and borrowing a framing because it sounded right

_log: THE SOWING LOG IS THIS STREET'S OWN, out of its changelog. A glasshouse keeps a log of what was sown and what came up wrong, and this one is the street's: times a model's trough showed, and who or what caught it, and the other way round. Every entry names the changelog entry where it was written up, by id, and `holds` is words that entry has; make-learning-large.py reads changelog.html and refuses an entry whose id or words are not there, the Community Center's rule. The changelog is never edited to make this agree: an entry that stops matching is fixed here. `caught` is who or what noticed, `now` what holds it today. The dates are the entries'. Nothing here is a tally of anybody's mistakes, and nobody is ranked by them.

log.title: A book from memory
log.came: A link to a book on the Hermitage's shelf was assembled from memory, and pointed at a different work, in the very file whose own header says not to do that.
log.caught: Asking Open Library about every link in that file.

log.title: Licences from memory

log.title: A framing that sounded kind
log.came: The Outskirts opened carrying the real-world reading of an edge of town, the place people get pushed out to. Our town accepts everybody, so it has no outside to push anybody to.
log.caught: Ryan, reading it. No checker could have: the argument was wrong only in context.
log.now: It is written into the street's house notes, where the next turning meets it first.
holds: no checker on this street can see an argument that is wrong only in context

log.title: A fence that said kept out
log.came: The edge of Helen Edgar's own gardens, in the Garden, was drawn as a woven fence.
log.caught: Helen, on a drawing of her own gardens.
log.now: Ivy and stars. A fence says kept out; ivy says this is as far as we can see.
holds: Ivy says THIS IS AS FAR AS WE CAN SEE

log.title: A credit from memory
log.came: A passage in our Sleep entry was nearly credited to the wrong Autistic writer, from memory. It is Sarah Kurchak's.
log.caught: Resolving every author against a library record.
log.now: Nobody on the street is credited from memory.
holds: nearly credited it to somebody else from memory

log.title: Open meant the wrong thing
log.came: Cavendish Coworking opened as a glass office with every door propped wide, as if transparency were an open floor plan.
log.now: A house where every door is shut and none is locked, and a tool that refuses the open-plan vocabulary.
holds: glass office with every door propped wide
transparency does not mean an open floor plan

log.title: What nobody screenshots
log.came: The skip link, the first thing a keyboard reaches on every page, was unreadable in room after room, yellow on yellow in some. Nobody had seen it, because it is off the screen until it has the focus.
log.caught: A checker that renders every page and measures every word against what is actually under it.
log.now: It is one of the checks that run before anybody commits a change here.
holds: nobody screenshots a focused skip link

log.title: The box was right and the screen was wrong
log.came: The Playhouse's new toys answered in a place off the screen, so they looked broken while every check said they worked.
log.caught: Ryan, pressing the toys he had asked for an hour earlier.
log.now: Every toy answers on the tile you pressed.
holds: every check, ours included, was reading the box

_street: The one sentence from How this site is made that the sowing log stands on, looked for in design.html on every build: that page is this street's own account of how it is built, and a room repeating it has to keep agreeing with it.

street.said: Checkers catch what can be checked. People looking at the page catch the rest, and several faults on this street were found by Ryan simply pressing the buttons.
